sentences.text: The genus Embaphias is known only from three incomplete vertebrae, one of which is flattened front-to-back and features a distinct circular outline.
A large vascular foramen sits below the articular rim of the cervical centrum, which measures 84 mm in transverse diameter, 78 mm in vertical diameter, and 45 mm in side length.
This vertebra possesses a pair of moderately developed diapophyses on its lateral sides that point vertically.
Three incomplete plesiosaur vertebrae were collected in 1893 by John H. Charles from the Pierre Formation in Great Bend of the Missouri River, South Dakota.
Edward Drinker Cope named the genus based on these three cervical vertebrae and described the fossils as a new genus and species, Embaphias circulosus, in 1894.
The generic name Embaphias is derived from the Greek word for 'saucer', while the specific name circulosus comes from the Latin word for 'circle' or 'ring'.
Embaphias is currently classified as a dubious genus of plesiosaur.
Its parent group is Plesiosauria, and it belongs to the class Reptilia.
Embaphias lived during the Late Cretaceous (Campanian) period.
Williston and Moodie (1917) suggested the fossils belong to its own genus based on the age and concavity of the vertebrae.
